coaching.title: Today's Run
coaching.message: Easy 4–5 miles, Z2 only (140–150 bpm), rolling terrain if available. Your resting HR is 7.5 bpm above your 30-day average and your recovery score sits at 46/100—both yellow flags that your nervous system is still in a debt cycle. This is taper week 20 with 18 days to race; the priority is *shedding fatigue*, not maintaining fitness. Keep it conversational, no tempo, no vert work today. You've already logged nearly 3 miles this morning; if you feel flat, dial this back to 3 miles or swap for a walk.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: Nail carbohydrates today: target 6–8g/kg body weight (roughly 420–560g for a 70kg runner) distributed across 4–5 meals. Your sleep efficiency last night was 70%, which is solid but not optimal for a taper week—glycogen repletion and steady glucose intake will support both recovery and central nervous system stability. Front-load carbs at breakfast and lunch, add a rice or pasta-based dinner, and include a simple carb source (banana, rice cakes, honey) with your afternoon pre-run fuel. Avoid large fats or fibre immediately around your run window.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Sleep is the single lever you control right now. Aim for 9+ hours tonight—you're getting 8.3h on average, which is fine for build phases but insufficient for a taper when your system is clearing a fatigue debt. Your elevated resting HR suggests sympathetic dominance; prioritize cool bedroom (65°F/18°C), no screens after 21:00, and consider a 15–20 minute walk this evening to downregulate. No ice baths, no aggressive foam rolling today—passive recovery only.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: You're 18 days out and entering the hardest phase of a taper: the doubt phase. Your training volume has dropped 94% in one week (48.8 → 2.9 miles). This is *correct* and *necessary*, but it will feel wrong. Use these next 18 days to visualize the Julian Alps course profile—2,500m vert over 50K means sustained climbing at 5–8% grades with sparse aid. Your aerobic base is locked in. Now rest, fuel, and build confidence that your body will respond when it matters.
